newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: BASF, PETRONAS SIGN $700 MLN VENTURE.
newsitem.headline: BASF, PETRONAS SIGN $700 MLN VENTURE.

text.p: Germany's BASF AG and Malaysia's state-owned oil company Petronas on Friday signed a $700 million joint venture agreement to build and operate a petrochemicals plant in Malaysia's central state of Pahang.
Under the agreement, BASF will have a 60 percent interest in the joint venture with Petronas taking the remaining 40 percent, a Petronas statement said.
The two companies will build an acrylic acid plant with capacity of 160,000 tonnes per annum which is expected to begin operations in the year 2000.
They will also operate an oxo-alcohols complex which will produce 80,000 tonnes per annum of 2-ethyl hexanol, 40,000 tonnes per annum of phtalic anhydride and 100,000 tonnes of plasticisers.
The oxo-alcohols complex is scheduled to come onstream in 2001.
Propylene, which is a main feedstock for both plants, will be supplied by a plant to be built by Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) in Gebeng, Pahang.
The chemicals produced by the plants will cater to industries like dispersions for coatings and paints, adhesives as well as for the paper, textile and leather industries.
